A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSMP research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material are readable and support comparison across relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original trailer-generation experiments, a 25-participant user study, and ablations in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds encoder, model-depth, self-correction, and movie-subgroup analyses.

M1.justification: The masked-prediction objective, scheduler, Algorithm 1, and post-processing remain unchanged. However, v3's supplementary Section 9 says a five-layer model is adopted, while Section 4.1 still specifies four layers, as v1 did. This conflict prevents a reliable determination of whether the default model changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use CMTD, Test-8, Test-74, Test-2024, and their Test-ALL combination for trailer generation. v3's period and genre results subdivide existing coverage; the revised dataset-size description and newly disclosed user-study details do not establish new coverage.

E2.justification: The original benchmark and user-study comparator sets are retained. v3 adds evaluated SigLIP2 and DINOv3 encoder alternatives in Table 9 and a Greedy comparison under relaxed matching in Table 10; TGT also participates in the new architecture-controlled comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 replaces the stated extension of 200 recent movies, including 30 Test-2024 pairs, with an extension comprising those 30 test pairs. This is a reported sample-size revision, without evidence that retained experiments were rerun. New appendix experiments vary encoders and model depth and align architectural dimensions with TGT; the original metrics and training budget remain stated unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the original ablations, v3 examines encoder dependence, architecture-matched bidirectional versus autoregressive modeling, depth sensitivity, and performance by movie period and genre. It also adds a 76-shot trailer's remasking/revision analysis and a relaxed-matching self-correction comparison (Tables 9–12 and Figure 6), substantially broadening diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and average user-study scores without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The added movie counts and per-position revision counts do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 retain their numerical results, while v3 adds substantial results on encoders, model capacity, relaxed Greedy decoding, and movie subgroups. For example, Table 11 reports F1 of 0.1710 for five-layer SSMP versus 0.1240 for TGT under the new comparison setting. Table 10's self-corrective values match the existing Table 7 R=2 row after rounding, despite prose mentioning deviation 3; they do not establish a new performance gain.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 and the mathematical reasoning are retained, with no new proofs or formal assumptions. The supplement's explicit identification of the initial hidden state and normalized FFN input clarifies existing notation rather than changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and superiority claims: bidirectional masked trailer generation, self-paced training, and progressive self-correction. The new appendix evidence supports these claims without redefining their main scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of selective remasking, attributes depth effects to under- and over-fitting, and links period/genre performance to training-data composition and narrative variability. It also states that the proposed mechanisms cannot directly transfer to autoregressive models. The original visual-only and limited-training-data limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly discloses participant ages of 10–52, the three user-study movies, and the viewing/rating arrangement, and identifies the SigLIP2 and DINOv3 checkpoints. Its abstract now advertises code as well as demos at the existing link. These are additional disclosures; they do not establish changes to the original user study.

R1.justification: The bibliography and main related-work discussion remain unchanged. Supplementary Section 9 adds limited positioning of ImageBind against image-based SigLIP2/DINOv3 and distinguishes the applicability of SSMP's mechanisms from autoregressive approaches.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v3 corrects author/contact text, adds an acknowledgement and a user-study subsection, clarifies architectural notation, and extends the supplementary discussion without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adds four distinct analytical tables (9–12) and the two-panel remasking/revision Figure 6, substantially expanding the supplementary displays. Existing tables and figures are retained but redistributed, the author block is compacted, and Figure 3's method legend is corrected from SPMG to SSMP.

improvement.justification: The encoder controls, subgroup analyses, and concrete user-study details modestly strengthen the evidence and make the study easier to assess. However, the conflicting four-versus-five-layer descriptions and the unexplained deviation-3 wording alongside rounded R=2 results weaken reproducibility of the additions. The unchanged main findings gain useful support, but these unresolved inconsistencies limit the overall improvement.
